# ETH-USD Technical Report (as of 2026-10-21)

**Data note:** The latest completed daily bar is 2026-10-20. The 2026-10-21 row came back "N/A" in every indicator series, so the 10-21 session is not yet in the data. All exact figures below come from the verified snapshot, and the individual indicator series match it with no discrepancies. The N/A rows are labeled "weekend or holiday," which doesn't apply to a 24/7 asset. I read it as the current day not yet being posted.

## Indicators selected (8) and why

| Indicator | Role |
|---|---|
| close_200_sma | Long-term trend regime |
| close_50_sma | Medium-term trend and dynamic resistance |
| close_10_ema | Short-term momentum and entry timing |
| macd | Trend momentum and zero-line regime |
| macdh | Momentum acceleration, early signal on MACD turns |
| rsi | Overbought/oversold and momentum regime |
| boll (with upper and lower bands from the snapshot) | Mean level and volatility envelope |
| atr | Volatility for stops and sizing |

I skipped VWMA and the separate MACD signal call. The snapshot already supplies the MACD signal and the Bollinger bands. VWMA would largely duplicate the moving-average trend information.

## Verified snapshot (2026-10-20 close)

- **OHLC:** open 2404.82, high 2474.20, low 2372.89, **close 2446.73**, volume about 11.05B.
- **Moving averages:** 10 EMA 2450.87, 50 SMA 2549.95, 200 SMA 2151.25.
- **Momentum:** RSI 43.15, MACD -47.17, MACD signal -31.62, histogram -15.55.
- **Bollinger:** middle 2532.26, upper 2773.87, lower 2290.65.
- **ATR:** 92.65, about 3.8% of the close (my arithmetic).

## Trend structure

**Long-term: constructive.**
- The 200 SMA rose steadily from 2079.65 (09-21) to 2151.25 (10-20).
- Price sits about 295 points above it.
- The 50 SMA is about 399 points above the 200 SMA, so the "golden-cross" structure is intact.
- The price history shows how this formed. ETH closed at 1916.46 on 08-18, then 2251.46 on 08-19 on about 29.6B volume, the heaviest in the sample. It has held the roughly 2,400–2,800 area since. The peak close was 2776.47 on 09-21 (high 2805.50).

**Medium-term: weakening.**
- Price (2446.73) is below the 50 SMA (2549.95) and below the Bollinger midline (2532.26).
- The 50 SMA peaked at 2556.17 on 10-11 and has since edged down to 2549.95. It is flattening rather than clearly falling.
- The 10-07 and 10-08 drop from 2697.52 to 2471.91, on about 20B volume each day, broke the late-September consolidation (about 2,670–2,727 closes).
- Since then price has made lower closes. The lowest was 2399.80 on 10-17, and the lowest low was 2320.55 on 10-15.

**Short-term: stabilizing, not yet reversing.**
- The 10 EMA fell from 2692.12 (10-06) to 2450.87 and has flattened. It was 2451.78 the day before.
- The 10-20 close (2446.73) is essentially on the 10 EMA, a bit below it.
- Closes since 10-14 have ranged between 2399.80 and 2496.63. That is a tight, directionless range, not a rebound.

## Momentum

- **MACD** peaked at 97.52 on 09-23, crossed below zero between 10-10 (+3.23) and 10-11 (-2.07), and is now -47.17. It is below its signal line (-31.62), so the bearish state is intact.
- **Histogram:** the trough was about -36.7 (10-10) and it is now -15.55. It has narrowed for several straight sessions (-29.4 on 10-16, -24.8 on 10-18, -21.6 on 10-19). The MACD line itself ticked up from -49.35 to -47.17. This is a loss of downside momentum, not a bullish crossover. A real signal would need the histogram to turn positive.
- **RSI** is 43.15. It fell from 72.18 on 09-21 to 37.41 on 10-08 and has stayed between about 37 and 45 since. It never reached oversold (30) and has not shown a bullish divergence. A range of 37–45 is typical of a downtrend. A move back above about 50–60 would be the first sign of regime change, and a drop through 30–35 would be the bearish extension.

## Volatility and risk

- **ATR** is 92.65 and has been drifting in a 78–104 band over the window. The latest value is mid-range, so there is no volatility expansion or contraction signal.
- **Bollinger Bands:** price (2446.73) is in the lower half, between the lower band (2290.65) and the midline (2532.26). It has not touched the lower band, so there is no oversold-extreme signal. The midline has been falling for about two weeks, from 2683.93 (10-07) to 2532.26. That confirms the downward drift.
- **Sizing example:** a stop at 1.5–2× ATR is about 139–185 points, roughly 5.7–7.6% of price. Position size should scale to that distance.

## Reference levels (not validated by past bounces)

These are levels from the tool output, not confirmed support or resistance.

- **Upside:**
  - 2532.26 (Bollinger midline)
  - 2549.95 (50 SMA)
  - 2534.70 (10-11 close)
  - 2576.58 (10-12 high)
- **Downside:**
  - 2399.80 (10-17 close)
  - 2320.55 (10-15 low)
  - 2290.65 (lower band)
  - 2151.25 (200 SMA)

## Scenarios

- **Bearish continuation (somewhat favored by the structure):** price below the 50 SMA and midline, MACD below its signal and zero, and RSI capped under 45. A close below 2399.80 or 2320.55 would open a test of the lower band near 2290 and eventually the rising 200 SMA near 2150. A break under the 200 SMA would damage the long-term regime.
- **Recovery:** the histogram turns positive, the MACD line crosses its signal, RSI breaks above about 50, and price reclaims the midline and 50 SMA (about 2530–2550). Until then, rallies into that zone face overhead supply.
- **Chop:** the narrowing histogram, flat 10 EMA, and tight closes suggest sideways trade between about 2,400 and 2,500 is possible before the next directional move.

## Cautions

- The 10-21 session is not reflected in any figure here.
- Momentum is improving (histogram) while trend is not. Mixed signals call for confirmation, not anticipation.
- Volume has been lower recently (about 5.9–11.1B over 10-17 to 10-20) than during the 10-07 and 10-08 selloff (about 20B). That is a fact about the data, and I can't tell from it whether selling pressure has really faded.
- I have no fundamental, on-chain, or news data. This is technical analysis only, and I am not making the trade decision.

## Summary table

| Item | Value / Reading | Interpretation |

| Last close (10-20) | 2446.73 | Mid-to-lower Bollinger range |
| 10 EMA | 2450.87 | Price at or slightly below; flattening |
| 50 SMA | 2549.95 | Price below; slope flat to slightly down |
| 200 SMA | 2151.25 | Price above; slope rising; long-term trend intact |
| 50 vs 200 SMA | 50 above 200 by about 399 | Bullish long-term structure |
| MACD / signal | -47.17 / -31.62 | Bearish; below zero and below signal |
| MACD histogram | -15.55 (trough about -36.7 on 10-10) | Downside momentum fading, no crossover yet |
| RSI | 43.15 | Bearish-neutral; range 37–45 since 10-08 |
| Bollinger (L / M / U) | 2290.65 / 2532.26 / 2773.87 | Price below falling midline; not oversold |
| ATR | 92.65 (about 3.8% of price) | Mid-range volatility; stop at 1.5–2× is about 139–185 |
| Upside reference levels | 2532 / 2550 / 2577 | Midline, 50 SMA, 10-12 high |
| Downside reference levels | 2400 / 2321 / 2291 / 2151 | 10-17 close, 10-15 low, lower band, 200 SMA |
| Bias | Medium-term bearish-to-neutral within a long-term uptrend | Wait for histogram and RSI confirmation or a break of 2,400 |
| Data caveat | 10-21 bar missing | Figures are through 10-20 |

**Overall Sentiment:** **Mixed** (Score: 4.4/10)
**Confidence:** Low

**Data coverage and limits (read first).** Two of four sources are unavailable. The Yahoo Finance news feed returned DATA_UNAVAILABLE, and the Reddit fetch failed for r/ethereum, r/CryptoCurrency and r/CryptoMarkets. Neither outage says anything about ETH-USD itself, so I did not estimate institutional-news or Reddit sentiment. The read below rests on 8 StockTwits messages and a 23-post sample from X (98 were fetched; the retrieval model selected the sample). Confidence is low. One X author (@TedPillows) accounts for about 11 of the 23 sampled posts, which skews the X sample toward a single technical view.

**1. StockTwits (retail, fast signal; n=8 on-topic messages).**
- The header and the per-message tags disagree. User tags: 4 Bullish (50%), 2 Bearish (25%), 2 unlabeled. The Jev classifier's read of the same posts: 2 bullish, 3 bearish, 1 neutral, 2 unclear.
- The gap comes from posts like @Ethmaxipad's. It is tagged Bullish, but the text ("this is shit… endured all of October… ain't even a little scared") reads as a holder defending a losing position, not a fresh bullish thesis.
- Bullish content is thin and mostly price-level talk: @Web30 "$3400 key here" and "alts blue skies activation", and @tequilamezcal "needs to break 2500 decisively if not back to 2300".
- Bearish and distressed content: @Eretheum ("fucking wrecked tomorrow", "no gains"), @flopy (negative), and @truthG (unlabeled), who describes being trapped at much higher prices and feeling hurt. This points to underwater holders and bag-holder frustration.
- @cubano1 asking "Who thinks we see 5k this year" shows retail still has long-dated upside hopes, but it is a question, not a conviction.
- Net: roughly split to slightly negative once the classifier is weighed. With n=8, this is directional only.

**2. X / Twitter (real-time traders, analysts, news accounts; sample of 23 of 98).**
- Price context: ETH is around $2,450–$2,500 (@WatcherGuru "$2,500 $ETH" with 2,814 likes, the highest engagement in the sample). The BitMine stake of 159,728 ETH for $390.6M implies about $2,445.
- Technical tone (@TedPillows, the most active voice):
  - Cautious or bearish. "ETH wants to go down… buyers disappearing… could revisit $2,150–$2,200" (10/20).
  - "Spot demand still weak; rally mostly short covering; large buyers waiting around $2,200–$2,250" (10/19).
  - "Weekly close below May highs… a bit concerning" (10/19).
  - "Back above $2,450 but looking weak; until $2,550 is reclaimed, risk of another sharp correction" (10/21).
  - There were mild constructive notes. On 10/15 he said ETH swept lows at $2,315 (top of the weekly bull market support band) and bounced to $2,450 (RSI 34→41). On 10/20 he said "spot buyers are waking up; a daily close above $2,450 is needed". He also called the area a "good accumulation zone" for long-term holders.
  - @byte_drift1 (10/17) echoes the weakness: lost $2,550, below the April highs, $2,450 is the key level.
- Flows (factual, from SoSoValue, Cointelegraph, Lookonchain and WuBlockchain):
  - US spot ETH ETFs saw net outflows of $26.13M on Oct 20, the fifth consecutive day of outflows.
  - Lookonchain's 7-day ETH ETF net flow is -155,122 ETH (-$384M), and the Oct 21 one-day flow is -$31.4M.
  - BTC ETFs show 7-day inflows of about +$212M. @TedPillows (10/20) said ETFs sold $103M of ETH while buying $526M of BTC the prior day and that "liquidity is moving out of alts and into Bitcoin."
  - This is a relative-weakness signal for ETH versus BTC from institutional wrappers.
- Supportive events:
  - Tom Lee's BitMine staked another 159,728 ETH ($390.6M). Its total staked is 5.23M ETH ($12.78B), or 86.5% of holdings. It also bought $30.4M last week, the 68th consecutive week of buying. This is a steady treasury bid that reduces liquid supply, and it was the most widely amplified fundamental item (Cointelegraph, Lookonchain, The Block).
  - Santiment data shows derivatives open interest recovering with prices, at $15.5B for ETH.
  - @TedPillows noted strong Binance bidding on 10/15.
- Leverage risk: a whale opened a $92M ETH long at 14x and was only about $64 from liquidation (10/15). Rising open interest after a bounce means a crowded-positioning risk in both directions.
- Promotional or low-credibility items to discount: @cryptocupra's "Tom Lee predicts $62,000… buying ETH now is like BTC in 2014" is hype with no sourcing. @fundstrat ("Ethereum keeps winning") is Tom Lee's firm, which is affiliated with the BitMine position and therefore not neutral. @TedPillows' "Imagine this…" has no content.

**3. Cross-source alignment and divergences.**
- Alignment: StockTwits (trapped holders, 2300/2500 level talk) and X technicians (weak bounce, $2,450–$2,550 resistance, $2,150–$2,300 downside zone) agree on the key price levels and on a fragile, unconvinced market. Both also show long-term bulls waiting for a reclaim.
- Divergence: the headline-style X posts (BitMine staking, "keeps winning", $62k calls) are bullish and promotional. The flow data (five straight days of ETF outflows) and the technical commentary lean bearish. Treasury buying and staking look like a steady bid from one large, vocal holder, while broader institutional ETF demand is weakening.
- Missing: no news or Reddit data, so there is no check on whether mainstream or holder-community framing diverges from X and StockTwits.

**4. Dominant narrative themes.**
- (a) Key levels: $2,450 and $2,550 as resistance, and $2,150–$2,300 as the pullback or accumulation zone.
- (b) ETH ETF outflows versus BTC inflows, and rotation out of alts.
- (c) BitMine/Tom Lee as persistent buyer and staker.
- (d) Retail fatigue and trapped holders after a weak October.
- (e) Leverage and short-covering driven bounces.

**5. Catalysts and risks surfaced.**
- Upside: a daily or weekly close above $2,450 and then $2,550; an end to the ETF outflow streak; continued BitMine buying and staking; further short squeezes.
- Downside: a weekly close below $2,450 and a "flush" toward $2,150–$2,250; continued ETF outflows; BTC dominance rotation; liquidation cascades from crowded leverage (open interest recovering to $15.5B, with the 14x whale example).
- Not covered by the data: no macro, regulatory or protocol-upgrade headlines, because the news feed was unavailable.

**6. Bottom line.** Sentiment is mixed with a slightly negative tilt. Retail is split and fatigued, technical commentary is cautious, and ETF flows are negative. A large treasury buyer and bullish promotional chatter offset these. This is a sentiment read only, not a price call, and it should be weighed against technicals and fundamentals. The sample is small and partly one-author, so confidence is low.

| Signal | Direction | Source | Evidence |

| Retail split (user tags) | Mixed/Neutral | StockTwits | 4 Bullish / 2 Bearish / 2 unlabeled (n=8), but tag text is often defensive |

| Technical weakness at $2,450–$2,550 | Mildly Bearish | X | @TedPillows (many posts), @byte_drift1; risk of drop to $2,150–$2,250 |

| Rotation from alts into BTC | Bearish (relative) | X | @TedPillows: ETFs sold $103M ETH, bought $526M BTC |
| BitMine staking and weekly buying | Bullish | X | 159,728 ETH ($390.6M) staked; 5.23M total (86.5%); 68th week of buying |

| Promotional hype ($62k, "keeps winning") | Bullish but low-credibility | X | @cryptocupra, @fundstrat (affiliated with BitMine) |

# ETH-USD: Weekly News and Macro Report (2026-10-14 to 2026-10-21)

## 1. Data coverage

| Source | Status |
|---|---|
| ETH-USD news (`get_news`) | **Unavailable.** The vendor has no articles tagged ETH-USD. This says nothing about the asset. |
| FRED macro series (fed funds, 10y, CPI, unemployment, VIX) | **Unavailable.** The FRED API key is not configured, so I have no actual rate, inflation, labor or volatility readings. |
| Global news | Available, but headline-only and equity-heavy. |
| Prediction markets (Polymarket) | Available for Fed, Ethereum and recession topics. |

I have no ETH price, volume, ETF-flow, on-chain or protocol news for this week. The macro view below rests on prediction markets and equity headlines only. I have not estimated any missing figures.

## 2. Macro backdrop

**Fed policy: on hold.**
- Polymarket prices "no Fed rate cuts in 2026" at **97%** ($9.0M volume, the deepest market in the set). The 1-week change is +0.1pp.
- Every alternative with 6 to 12 cuts is priced at about 0%.
- Traders should not expect easing as a liquidity catalyst before year-end. I cannot confirm the current fed funds level or the inflation and labor data behind this, because FRED was unavailable.

**Recession risk: low.**
- US recession by end of 2026 is priced at **8%** ($2.3M volume).
- UK and Japan recession odds are about 4% each, but those markets are very thin (about $16K and $4K volume), so I would not rely on them.
- The market is not pricing a growth scare, which is consistent with the risk-on equity tone.

**Equities and cross-asset (headlines only, no index levels):**
- Q3 earnings season is under way. Headlines describe the S&P 500 and Nasdaq gaining, led by Meta, Tesla and SpaceX (ticker "SPCX"), and the Dow rising.
- IBM beat Q3 revenue and EPS estimates, helped by software strength and a recovery in delayed contracts.
- Gold futures edged higher as oil prices retreated (WSJ). Falling oil eases inflation pressure at the margin.
- Metals and mining headlines (silver and zinc production, antimony and defense demand) show commodity activity but nothing crypto-specific.

## 3. Ethereum: what prediction markets imply

| Market (by Dec 31, 2026) | Probability | Volume | 1-week change |
|---|---|---|---|
| Dip to $2,250 | **59%** | $1.5M | **-8.5pp** |
| Dip to $1,500 | 9% | $3.2M | -0.1pp |
| Dip to $1,000 | 2% | $2.4M | -4.5pp |
| Dip to $800 | 1% | $1.7M | -2.0pp |
| Reach $3,500 | 16% | $1.0M | not reported |
| Reach $10,000 | 1% | $0.9M | -0.1pp |

- **Spot is probably above $2,250.** A 59% chance of dipping to $2,250 suggests ETH has not recently traded there, but this is an inference. I have no spot quote.
- **Downside odds are falling.** The $2,250 dip probability fell 8.5pp this week, and the $1,000 and $800 dip odds also dropped. That points to easing fear of a deep drawdown or a modest improvement in sentiment. It is one week of data on mid-volume markets, so treat it as a tilt rather than a signal.
- **The distribution is skewed to range-bound.**
  - Tail crash scenarios ($1,000 or below) are priced at 2% or less.
  - A move to $3,500 is priced at 16%.
  - A move to $10,000 is priced at 1%.
  - Taken together, the market expects ETH to stay inside a broad $1,500 to $3,500 band through year-end, with a better-than-even chance of a retest of $2,250.

## 4. Trading implications

1. **No Fed-driven upside catalyst.** With 97% odds of no cuts, ETH upside has to come from crypto-native flows. I cannot verify those this week.
2. **Risk-on equities help but do not confirm.** Strong earnings and rising indices are supportive for high-beta assets. Without ETH price data I cannot say whether crypto is following.
3. **The $2,250 level matters.** At 59% odds it is the market's central reference. If spot trades near it, the dip market suggests support there is more likely tested than not. Confirm the current price first.
4. **Low recession risk reduces macro tail risk.** An 8% recession probability and no sign of a growth shock argue against macro-driven liquidation, but I could not check the VIX or credit conditions.
5. **Position sizing.** Given the data gaps, any trade should rest on price, volume and flow data from another source.

## 5. Gaps to fill before trading

- ETH spot price, 7-day range, volume and funding or open interest.
- Spot ETH ETF flows and any regulatory or staking news.
- Actual FRED readings for fed funds, 10y yield, CPI, unemployment and VIX.
- Upcoming macro dates such as FOMC and CPI releases. I did not verify the calendar.

## 6. Summary table

| Area | Finding | Source / confidence | Trading read |

| ETH-USD news | No data returned | Vendor unavailable | Blind on asset-specific catalysts |
| Fed policy | 97% no cuts in 2026 | Polymarket, $9.0M volume (high) | No easing tailwind |

| FRED macro data | Unavailable | API key missing | Rates, inflation and labor unverified |
| Equities | Indices up on Meta, Tesla, SpaceX, IBM earnings | Headlines only (medium) | Supportive risk tone |
| Gold / oil | Gold up as oil retreats | WSJ headline | Mild disinflation, safe-haven bid |
| ETH $2,250 dip | 59%, down 8.5pp | Polymarket, $1.5M volume (medium) | Likely retest, but odds are fading |
| ETH deep downside | $1,500 at 9%, $1,000 at 2%, $800 at 1% | Polymarket (medium-high) | Crash tail is small |

# ETH-USD Fundamental Report (as of 2026-10-21)

## 1. Scope and data limitations

ETH-USD (Ethereum USD, exchange: CCC) is a crypto asset, not a company. It has no balance sheet, income statement, cash flow statement, or insiders in the corporate sense. Here is what each tool returned:

| Tool | Result |
|---|---|
| get_fundamentals | Returned limited market data (below) |
| get_balance_sheet (quarterly) | NO_DATA_AVAILABLE |
| get_cashflow (quarterly) | NO_DATA_AVAILABLE |
| get_income_statement (quarterly) | NO_DATA_AVAILABLE |
| get_insider_transactions | No insider transactions reported |

I have not estimated or filled in any of the missing statement data. The empty insider result reflects the absence of corporate insiders. It is not evidence of a bullish or bearish signal.

## 2. Data available from the tools

- **Market cap:** about $298.1B USD
- **52-week high:** $4,250.67
- **52-week low:** $1,506.51
- **50-day average:** $2,549.95
- **200-day average:** $2,151.25

The tool did not return a current spot price, so I cannot say exactly where ETH-USD trades today.

## 3. What the numbers imply

1. **Implied price level.** I do not have the circulating supply from the tool. If supply is about 120–121M ETH (my assumption, not tool output), a $298.1B market cap implies a price of roughly $2,450–2,480. That would place it slightly below the 50-day average and above the 200-day average. Treat this as an approximation and verify it against a live price.
2. **Trend.** The 50-day average ($2,549.95) is about 18.5% above the 200-day average ($2,151.25). This is a bullish medium-term structure: shorter-term averages sit above longer-term ones, which suggests recovery momentum over the past several months.
3. **Range position.** The 52-week range is wide, from $1,506.51 to $4,250.67. The high is about 1.7x the low. If the implied price near $2,450 is right, ETH-USD sits roughly 42% below the high and about 63% above the low. That points to a large drawdown from the peak with only a partial recovery.
4. **Volatility.** The range shows large swings, so position sizing and risk limits matter.

## 4. Fundamentals this toolset cannot measure

Traders should get the following from other sources, such as on-chain analytics, protocol dashboards, and ETF flow data:

- Network activity: transactions, active addresses, and fee revenue
- Fee burn (EIP-1559) versus issuance, and net supply change
- Staking: share of supply staked, validator count, and staking yield
- Layer-2 activity and its effect on mainnet fee capture
- ETF and institutional flows, and exchange balances
- DeFi total value locked and stablecoin supply on Ethereum
- Regulatory developments and the protocol upgrade roadmap

## 5. Takeaways for traders

- The tools support only a technical-style view (moving averages and range), not a fundamental valuation. No earnings, cash flow, or balance sheet analysis is possible.
- The 50-day average above the 200-day average is a constructive medium-term signal. The large distance below the 52-week high suggests resistance overhead.
- The $2,150–2,550 band (between the two averages) is a reasonable zone to watch for support. This is a heuristic, not a tool-derived conclusion.
- Another agent should supply the current price, volume, on-chain metrics, and news flow before any trade decision is made.

## 6. Summary table

**Recommendation**: Underweight

**Rationale**: The bull's long-term structure is real. The 200 SMA is rising, the 50 SMA sits about 18.5% above it, and price has held the 2,400–2,800 range since August. That is why this is Underweight and not Sell. But the bear won on the evidence that matters for the next few weeks.

(1) The risk-reward math works against an entry here. The bull's tight stop, a close below 2,399.80, is only 1.9% away, about half an ATR, and price already closed there on 10-17. The wider 1.5–2x ATR stop risks 5.7–7.6% to reach a first target, the 50 SMA at 2,550, that is only 4.2% away. That pays about 0.55–0.75 per unit of risk. The bull's own accumulation zone (the swept 2,315 low down to the 200 SMA at 2,151) is 5–12% below the current 2,446.73. The bear also caught a bull error: the 52-week low is about 38% below spot, not 62%.

(2) Flows at the margin are negative. US spot ETH ETFs have seen five straight days of outflows, $384M over seven days, while BTC ETFs took in about $212M. BitMine's $30.4M of weekly buying offsets only about 8% of that, and its 159,728 ETH staking move locks up coins it already owned, so it adds no new demand.
